title: PR #899 build-cache performance log

comparability.flags_note: The matched reruns confirm GHC 9.8.4, -O1 and disabled split sections in the archived build logs for all three routes. Cabal and Nix are intended alternatives on the same declared workload, so route-level descriptive comparison is allowed. Exact equality of every package, compiler, linker and codegen default remains unconfirmed; cache and dependency state differ, so causal percentage claims remain unsupported.
comparability.ci_note: Run 36143308159 production jobs are still the unsplit candidate. Only its optional measurement jobs apply the split pilot. Its 8m36s production span is cache-rate-limited/disabled and is not evidence that the pilot is faster.
comparability.total_rule: For a multi-stage workload, sum stages within each repetition first, then take the median of those per-repetition totals. Never sum stage medians and call that a total median.
comparability.matched_note: F-H are three n=3 Linux matched-workload points. All fresh, repeat and Text-edit routes have valid samples. The candidate Int-sibling route has one comparison_unusable cache audit and remains diagnostic only. Pilot Text realization is 298.890s versus candidate/unsplit 259.269s (+39.621s, +15.282%), so it fails the preset >=15% and >=60s representative-edit improvement criterion and does not justify expansion. Including the core test, the same route is 302.583s versus 262.835s.
comparability.cache_audit_note: Candidate audits: 11/12 valid; pilot audits: 12/12 valid. Every audit covers 10 outputs and 40 remote checks. Fresh/Text/sibling outputs are local-absent with remote-absent checks; repeat outputs are local-present with remote-absent checks. The candidate repetition-3 sibling audit retains one neohaskell.cachix.org network error. Add evaluation.eval_s to route stages; exclude probe_s and remaining audit wall time.

timeline_rule: Append each future change in chronological order. Plot each workload metric through measured events in timeline order; pending changes have no values. Connected lines describe measured history. Matched workload points support descriptive route comparison; they do not establish a causal percentage improvement.
comparison_caveat: Same workload; cache conditions and execution routes vary. Lines show observations, not isolated effects.
